text:
sam: quick follow-up from the attribution RFC meeting earlier — we still need a pragmatic approach for ad-hoc billing queries that doesn't explode query cost. thinking out loud: should we attach a low-cardinality `billing_key` early (ingest) or keep enrichment late and do joins at query time? :thinking:
anya: main worry is cardinality and join cost. if `billing_key` is high-cardinality we can't index everything. late-join avoids storing extra fields at ingest but makes queries expensive and unpredictable.
matt: two concrete tradeoffs i've seen: 1) pre-enrich small, stable keys at ingress (fast queries, higher ingest cost, needs reliable lookup service). 2) late enrichment via join to a mapping table (low ingest cost, higher query latencies and scan costs).
jia: can we do a hybrid? e.g., materialize a compact mapping for the 99% of traffic that's hot and fall back to late-join for the tail. that keeps common queries cheap.
sam: yeah hybrid seems promising. implementation idea: maintain a Kafka-backed changelog of tenant->billing_key mappings, build a small local cache (or redis) in the ingest path and stamp spans/envelopes with billing_key when cache hit. on miss, stamp with `billing_key: null` and record an enrichment task that backfills or marks for query-time join.
anya: metrics we'd need: cache hit ratio per minute, additional payload bytes per event, increased ingress CPU, and query rate/latency delta for ad-hoc joins. add alert if cache miss rate > 1% or if extra bytes push bandwidth above threshold.
matt: SQL sketch for fallback join:
```
SELECT count(1), b.billing_bucket
FROM spans s
LEFT JOIN billing_mapping b ON s.tenant_id = b.tenant_id
WHERE s.timestamp >= $1
GROUP BY b.billing_bucket;
```
Note: this assumes `tenant_id` is always present in span — if not, we'd need fallback stitching which is more expensive.
jia: for the materialized hot-table approach we could push a compact materialized view into clickhouse or our OLAP store and keep it partitioned by tenant hash. updates come from CDC stream. should keep retention short (30d) to limit size.
sam: rollout plan proposal:
- Phase 1: prototype cache-at-ingest for a handful of internal tenants, measure hit rate and extra bytes. (matt owner)
- Phase 2: build fallback join path and query cost budget guardrails + dashboard (jia owner)
- Phase 3: opt-in by customer route, expand cache coverage, add canary for large tenants. (anya owner)

anya: small UX question — how do we surface when a query used the fallback join vs cached billing_key? would be great to tag query traces.
matt: we can emit a query-side annotation `attribution_source={ingest_cached|late_join}` and include that in trace and billing logs. easy to add in the query planner.
observability-bot: noted: created ticket OBO-2489 to track Phase 1 prototype. assigned to matt, due 2w. :white_check_mark: 
sam: ok lets keep actions small. matt, can you drop a short design doc with cache TTL, eviction policy, and estimated mem footprint for 100k tenants by EOD tomorrow? jia, please mock a perf test that simulates 20% cold lookups and baseline join latencies. anya i'll coordinate customer opt-in UX.
anya: ack. i'll post a follow-up with dashboard wireframes and the alert thresholds. :thumbsup:
matt: will do — starting with a rough memory calc and simple redis prototype.
__notes: thread is a single continuous string of messages, timestamps are root and bounds. No title field per agents.md.
